additionalCoursework:
Other required courses:
-Writing/Speech: 2 courses (must emphasize written or verbal communication in the English language)
-Social Science: 1 course (can include Psychology, Sociology, Anthropology, Economics, Political Science, etc.)
-Humanities: 1 course (can include Art, Music, Dance, Theatre, History, Philosophy, Literature, Communication, etc.)

*Advanced Placement (AP), International Baccalaureate (IB), College Level Examination Program (CLEP), independent study, and correspondence courses do not satisfy these requirements and will not be counted. AP Chemistry credit earned with a score of 4 or 5 can fulfill one (1) semester of general chemistry. AP Chemistry credit must be posted on the official transcript in order to be counted.

For additional information, visit our website: https://medicine.utah.edu/programs/md/admissions/requirements

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The mission of the Office of Academic Culture and Community is to create a welcoming and respectful environment in academic medicine for people from all backgrounds, actively recruit and fully foster the development of a workforce that reflects our communities.

Our goals:

•	To lead efforts for cultural awareness and embrace and welcome cultural differences in the School of Medicine and the Utah community
•	To maintain educational continuum through medical school
•	To support partnerships within the School of Medicine and the entire Utah community
•	To create sustainable educational and health partnerships throughout the entire Utah community.
•	To embrace all medical students' volunteer efforts to serve the Utah community
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Information is available in the Medical Student Handbook.  Please visit the Student Affairs website at http://medicine.utah.edu/studentaffairs/
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: We have medical student interest groups ranging from specialty related, social, and service oriented groups. Medical students are encouraged to explore their interests and create their own students interest groups. A list of current student interest groups can be found here: https://medicine.utah.edu/students/involvement/interest-groups
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
In Utah, you can truly have it all. Salt Lake City and the surrounding areas offer newcomers diverse neighborhoods, great schools, arts and entertainment, and endless possibilities for sports and recreation. Work/life balance is an important element of the culture of our institution. We offer not just competitive programs of study but also a quality of life that's hard to beat. Whether you ski, bike, hike, or just walk, our outdoors scene is unparalleled, and the natural beauty of Utah draws visitors internationally. 

https://uofuhealth.utah.edu/why-utah

Housing & Residential Education creates an engaging community where students live, learn, and thrive. We develop a sense of belonging, provide opportunities for personal growth, and foster a safe and supportive environment. Our team aims to make the University of Utah feel like home.  https://www.housing.utah.edu/

Looking for your home off campus? Visit the following pages for more information on additional housing options including Family Housing https://apartments.utah.edu/ or Off-Campus Housing https://www.offcampushousing.utah.edu/listing
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The Wellness program provides individual counseling and support groups for all student populations, including underrepresented populations and gender and LGBTQIA+ students. These services are confidential, free, and accessible throughout medical school.  There are also several student interest groups. Student Affairs and Office of Academic Culture and Community provide individual student support, and sponsors Professional Excellence and Community Committee groups for each class. This student-led initiative holds class meetings that provide inclusivity, dialogue, and professionalism training.
Students looking for individual therapy, relationship therapy, single sessions, group support & medication management should fill out an interest form to schedule a Wellness Consult. The Medical Student Wellness Program offers programming that supports students’ well-being holistically including Wellness Check-Ins. For more information, visit https://medicine.utah.edu/students/wellness/services
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The Medical Student Wellness Program (MSWP) offers group support on a variety of topics. Students looking for individual therapy, relationship therapy, single sessions, group support and medication management should fill out an interest form to schedule a Wellness Consult. The MSWP also offers programming that supports students' well-being holistically, including Wellness Check-Ins. For more information on the wellness program and resources available, visit https://medicine.utah.edu/students/wellness/services
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
At the Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine at the University of Utah, campus culture is rooted in innovation, collaboration, and a deep commitment to advancing health and well-being. Nestled against the breathtaking Wasatch Mountains, the School of Medicine fosters an environment where academic excellence, inclusivity, and belonging intersect to create a vibrant and supportive community. 
 
Guided by the mission to advance health through excellence in education, research, and clinical care, the campus culture encourages students, faculty, and staff to thrive both personally and professionally.  
 
At our institution, we emphasize the importance of a well-rounded experience by providing robust support for interest groups, leadership development, and mentorship. The School of Medicine’s campus culture inspires future leaders in healthcare to collaborate, innovate, and address the complex needs of all populations.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: With the LIC curriculum change, students will be traveling to different clinics around the Salt Lake City area and beyond.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Academic Success Program (ASP) provides a comprehensive approach to medical student success.  ASP is committed to supporting medical students through tutoring, workshops, and learning resources.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Clinical work begins in year one. Students will spend one to two half days per week in student-led clinics. As students’ skills grow, they will assume more complex roles.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Second year includes Longitudinal Integrated Clerkships—like block rotations, but students care for patients, build relationships with preceptors, and gain competencies across many disciplines.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The curriculum is designed to produce highly skilled physicians who are technically proficient, caring, compassionate and capable of adapting to the changing health care demands of the 21st century. Active learning approaches and critical thinking skills are all a part of our educational environment. The MD program is organized into three phases and focuses on five content pillars: foundational sciences, clinical sciences, health systems sciences, health humanities, and professional identity formation.  With variable degrees of emphasis, these content pillars are integrated into the curriculum for all four years.  
 
https://medicine.utah.edu/programs/md/2023
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Post acceptance, students have the opportunity to apply for a primary care track. The primary care track gives students the opportunity to gain additional expertise in both rural and urban underserved primary care including a longitudinal integrated clerkship placement in a rural environment.  All students are placed in longitudinal integrated clerkships that include primary care and have the opportunity to participate in additional primary care electives following the clerkship year.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
The summer Medical Student Research Program (MSRP) is a competitive mentored research program. Medical students have the opportunity to work with basic science, clinical science, or health care research investigators. 

Goals are to enhance students' research horizons and develop scientific presentation and writing skills. Students whose projects are selected for support are paid a stipend from an NIH grant for their research activities. Students are expected to present a poster at an annual Research Forum, which their mentors attend and support their trainees. Students may apply for Travel funds to present their research findings at national meetings. Projects are eight weeks in length and students are expected to work approximately 40 hours/week minus release time to attend designated weekly research seminars. There is a monthly stipend paid for the eight week program. For more information, visit https://medicine.utah.edu/medresearch
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Rotations are performed at clinics & hospitals through 3 affiliations: 1) University of Utah Health Sciences. 2) Intermountain Healthcare, including Primary Children's Hospital. 3) Veteran's Affairs

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The SFESOM is Utah’s only academic medical center serving the Mountain West. It serves as the training ground for scientists and the majority of the state’s health care professionals. Learn more here: https://uofuhealth.utah.edu/about 

We're committed to you: your journey, goals, values, and knowledge. Our mission-driven MD program centers around relationships, community, and professionalism. SFESOM students graduate with real-world clinical skills, top-rate research education, strong professional identities, and experiences serving all populations in Utah and beyond. The program is organized into 3 phases and focuses on 5 content pillars: foundational sciences, clinical sciences, health systems sciences, health humanities sciences, and professional identity formation. Students are part of an intergenerational, academic House system, emphasizing relationships, coaching, and leadership. Learn more here: https://medicine.utah.edu/programs/md/2023
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine at the University of Utah serves all people and communities of Utah and the Mountain West by intentionally working to improve individual and community health outcomes and quality of life. This is achieved through excellence in patient care, education, and research by: 
-Purposefully educating physicians, scientists, and health care professionals to ensure compassionate, patient-centered care to all.
-Serving rural and underserved communities by addressing social determinants of health to decrease health disparities among all people.
-Engaging in scholarly research to advance knowledge, innovation, well-being, and health for all people.
-Fostering a culture of respect and community by recognizing outstanding contributions by students, trainees, staff, faculty, and community partners.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: 2 weeks, though maximum time allowed will vary depending on when the offer is made.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
A minimum of 3 letters must be submitted and received by the AMCAS Letter Service in order for applicants to receive a secondary application.  

Applicants are encouraged to request letters from those who know them well, who can speak to their abilities and experiences (academic and otherwise – leadership, service, personal growth, etc.), and can write a strong letter. Possible letter writers may include supervisors, mentors, professors, community leaders, or those who may have supervised or assisted with a long-term or most meaningful experience.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The SFESOM employs a matrix, applicants with MCAT total scores and undergraduate GPA within the following ranges are encouraged to apply to our program:

An MCAT total of 494- 497 and a GPA of 3.80 or higher
An MCAT total of 498-499 and a GPA of 3.60 or higher
An MCAT total of 500 and a GPA of 3.00 or higher

These requirements are subject to change, please review the SOM Office of Admissions website for the most up-to-date admissions requirements: https://medicine.utah.edu/admissions/
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: All applicants to the Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine at the University of Utah must meet the minimum MCAT and GPA requirements in order to be eligible for a secondary application. Upon meeting these requirements, the SFESOM Admissions Committee considers all aspects of the medical school application through a mission-aligned review process. Applicants must meet a variety of academic and activity requirements, as the balance of outside activities and responsibilities with school or work can be an indicator of one’s ability to navigate the personal and professional challenges they may face as a physician.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: All applicants are required to take the MCAT within four years of their matriculation to medical school. Only MCATs taken January 2023 - August 2026 will be considered for the 2026-2027 application cycle. We do not consider MCAT subsections and will only consider an applicant’s overall highest MCAT Total score.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Only an applicant's total cumulative undergraduate GPA as calculated by AMCAS will be considered. Post-Baccalaureate GPA is factored into the undergraduate GPA. Graduate GPA is not considered. To learn more about how AMCAS calculates GPA, please review the AMCAS Applicant Guide: https://students-residents.aamc.org/media/11616/download
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo:
Prerequisite courses must be taken for credit and a passing grade at a regionally accredited institution in the United States or Canada prior to matriculation to medical school. 

Courses completed through regionally accredited online institutions, two-year institutions, community colleges, and/or concurrent enrollment programs are also accepted.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: The Office of Admissions does not accept letters of intent. Once a Secondary Application has been submitted, no changes or updates can be made to the application. Any updates to an applicant's name, address, legal state, phone number, email, or other contact information must be updated through the AMCAS system.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: In addition to Federal Unsubsidized Stafford Loans, we also offer a limited number of institutional loans and scholarships each year. All awards are based on need. Financial aid supplements the contribution of the student and/or family, who are expected to provide the maximum assistance possible.

medSchoolPrograms.info: The Southern Utah Regional Medical Campus (SURMC) in St George, Utah, trains future physicians dedicated to advancing healthcare in rural Utah. Through a community-centered curriculum and hands-on experiences across the region, students gain the skills, knowledge, and compassion to become leaders in rural primary care and population health. SURMC students will be uniquely positioned in the community and have opportunities to work with rural health care providers around St George, Utah. Applications for the Southern Utah Regional Medical Campus open 05/01/2026 through 09/01/2026.  An MD cohort of 10 will be accepted, focusing on rural primary care and population health. Students accepted into the regional campus will spend their first year in Salt Lake City, then transfer to St George for the remainder of their medical education.

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation:
Applicants invited to interview will participate in group assessment in which evaluators will explore attributes such as: 
- Teamwork and Collaboration
- Reliability and Dependability
- Self-Directed Learning
- Interpersonal Skills

AAMC PREview® Exam Required - You must submit a PREview score for your application to be considered complete. Registration for PREview opens in January, and applicants are strongly encouraged to take the AAMC PREview Exam from March to July for priority consideration. The AAMC PREview Exam must be completed by August 2026 to be eligible to receive an interview invitation. Earlier test dates are highly encouraged as interview spots can/will fill up.

Applicants invited to interview will participate in two longer-form interviews in which evaluators will explore attributes such as:
- Motivation for seeking a medical degree
- Individual experiences
- Interpersonal and problem solving skills
- Understanding of medical ethics
- Awareness and understanding of the medical profession

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Applicants can complete the required prerequisite coursework at any accredited institution in the U.S. or Canada. All admissions requirements, including required courses and undergraduate degree, must be completed prior to matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Coursework does not expire; it is recommended that applicants contact their premedical advisor for assistance in planning the course work that meets necessary requirements, expectations, and criteria.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Legal residents of Utah and those who graduated from a Utah high school, college, or university are given preference but qualified out-of-state applicants are encouraged to apply. Applications are reviewed holistically, focusing on institutional mission alignment. Applicants are evaluated through experiences, secondary application essays, recommendation letters, PREview exam score, and interview assessments. In addition, the Southern Utah Regional Medical Campus seeks individuals with interest and experiences that support a commitment to primary care and rural Utah.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Working alongside physicians and other healthcare professionals is helpful in determining future career goals, and it is important that the applicant has a thorough understanding of what it is like to work in a healthcare setting as a practicing physician. This includes having an idea of how science is involved in patient care, as well as being comfortable around individuals who are physically and/or mentally ill. This knowledge is best obtained through a combination of direct patient care services and physician shadowing when possible.
